svg.title: One forward pass: from demonstration to weights
svg.desc: Animated forward pass of WIZARD in six steps. One instruction and one demonstration without action labels enter. The frozen pi0.5 encoder forms a 512-dimensional task representation. It expands into a structured grid of 5,929 adapter blocks. Predicted scale statistics restore each block's numerical range. The rank-16 LoRA adapter, 46.1 million parameters, plugs into the frozen pi0.5 backbone. The specialised policy then drives the robot. Adapter generation takes about 0.07 seconds and 1.74 GB on an A6000. Without motion, all six steps are shown lit.
svg.text: One forward pass: from demonstration to weights

g.text: Instruction and one demonstration go in
The demonstration is video only. There are no robot-action labels.
The frozen π0.5 encoder builds a task representation z
2,048-d features are projected to 512-d and aligned to a fixed length.
z expands into a structured grid of adapter blocks
5,929 blocks on a 16 × 512 grid, ordered by the part of the model they came from.
Predicted scale statistics restore each block's range
Parameter groups were normalised separately, so their magnitudes must be put back.
The rank-16 LoRA adapter plugs into the frozen π0.5
No gradient step on the target task. The backbone itself never changes.
The specialised policy drives the robot
The whole adapter was produced by a single forward pass of the generator.
One demonstration in, one specialised policy out
No action labels and no gradient updates on the target task.
About 0.07 s to generate the adapter, using 1.74 GB on an A6000

svg.text: Illustrative animation, not to time scale.
